title: Microsoft Purview Information Protection: File Labeler and File Viewer for macOS
summary: The briefing correctly reports Microsoft's rollout notice, existing label policies and per-user billing model. It incorrectly treats the account requirement as undocumented: Microsoft Learn says users must sign in with a Microsoft 365 work or school account to apply sensitivity labels. The publishing-policy path also stops at the start of the configuration wizard.

claims.claim: The feature is user-opt-in: the client is separately downloaded rather than pre-installed, with no documented prerequisite admin enablement switch.
claims.quote: The client will not be pre-installed and will need to be downloaded separately. ... Existing sensitivity labeling policies will continue to apply; no changes will be required.

Opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-protection-client, purview/create-sensitivity-labels and powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-labelpolicy; no macOS installation switch.

claims.claim: Opening protected files remains subject to authorization rather than bypassing the protection's access permissions.
claims.quote: Before encrypted content is rendered, successful authentication must occur for people who are authorized to open the file and given access to it. If authorization fails, the file doesn't open.

claims.claim: Advanced label-based protection for all files on devices is an endpoint DLP setting.
claims.quote: When you configure users for the endpoint data loss prevention setting Advanced label-based protection for all files on devices and use the information protection client

claims.claim: On Windows, this setting lets labeled and encrypted files other than Office and PDF retain their original file name extension on the device.
claims.quote: When a user selects a sensitivity label that applies encryption, the file name extension now doesn't change. As a result, there's no change to the user workflow because they can continue to view and edit the file in their standard application.

claims.claim: Without that setting, encrypting those files with the Windows client changes their file name extension.
claims.quote: When users label and encrypt these files with the information protection client and without this setting for advanced label-based protection: ... The encrypted file changes its file name extension and becomes read-only

claims.claim: Without that setting, those encrypted Windows files open in the information protection viewer instead of their original applications.
claims.quote: can no longer be opened by apps that support the original file name extension. Instead, the file opens in the Microsoft Purview Information Protection viewer.

claims.fix: The route correctly reaches the Create policy wizard but stops before label selection. Extend the printed path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label > Choose sensitivity labels to publish > Choose sensitivity labels to publish > Add'. Add to the existing note: 'Select the labels before Add, then follow the wizard prompts to select users and groups and complete the policy configuration.' Mirror this in the rendered table.
